positions.commentary: The speaker is not surprised to see Carvana down 70-80% and believes the market has correctly marked it down.
The speaker is not surprised to see Coinbase down 70-80% and believes the market has correctly marked it down.
The speaker states they never bought Netflix.
The speaker states that Alphabet is similar to Amazon in terms of looking expensive and potentially going to flame out like the dot-com bust.
Microsoft tried to beat Google with Bing but only achieved a single-digit market share despite spending billions.
The speaker values Amazon as a great business with a relatively certain future, but notes that valuing it on current earnings results in a very high multiple, around 90 times.

The speaker acknowledges Zuckerberg founded one of the most valuable businesses on earth and did good acquisitions like Instagram, but criticizes him for not reinvesting profits and being a 'jam today' guy.
Coca-Cola is trying to trick consumers that their sugar water is better than anybody else's, and brands like this are very vulnerable.
The speaker considers Apple's iPhone to be demonstrably a superior phone and implies that tech brands are much more durable because they are based on functionality.
The speaker notes that Disney has a great stream of profits from movies and theme parks that are valuable but not on the balance sheet.
The speaker describes American Express as a valuable trusted franchise with little assets that can earn money for many years.
The speaker mentions Adobe as one of the companies that look much more reasonably priced when adjusted for economic reality.
The speaker mentions Workday as one of the companies that look much more reasonably priced when adjusted for economic reality.
The speaker mentions a Swedish company called Evolution as something they recently started doing research on.
The speaker mentions Bezos spent heavily to build a logistics network that now competes against UPS and FedEx, taking market share from them.
